clue.text: Create air from Beethoven in recollection? Unable to recollect things

parts.note: to forge something is to create or fashion it

indicators.note: re-collection read as a backward gathering: the German word is picked up again from its far end

parts.note: Beethoven was German, and the German word for air is Luft

explanation.surface: A musician tries to write down a Beethoven melody from memory, but can't quite remember it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air from Beethoven' looks like a tune but is the German word for air; 'in recollection' reads it collected again from the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forgetful habitually fails to remember, so is unable to recall things.

clue.text: Inaccessible promotional material for electrical unit

parts.note: somewhere far away is hard to reach
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert for an electrical component is somehow impossible to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: The farad is the SI unit of electrical capacitance, named after Michael Faraday.

clue.text: This rogue reforms — becoming _________?

indicators.note: the letters are formed again into a new order, just as a reformed rogue is remade

explanation.surface: A villain mends their ways and becomes, as the blank invites you to fill in, virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the rogue who reforms becomes upright, and the letters of 'This rogue', reformed, fill the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformed villain turns virtuous and morally upright, which is the sense the blank asks for.

clue.text: Curse the amount senior manager gets?

parts.note: an exec is an executive
a ration is a fixed allowance or amount

explanation.surface: An envious employee grumbles about how much the boss is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'the amount an exec gets', the clue becomes an exec's ration.
explanation.definitionFit: An execration is an angry denunciation or oath, a noun sense of curse.

clue.text: Stupid articles probing passing craze

definitions.note: used here as a noun, a stupid person

indicators.note: the articles push into the craze, as a probe goes inside

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Some newspaper articles examine a short-lived trend in a dim-witted way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' is a noun here, as in 'Come here, stupid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a dimwit, someone the speaker calls stupid to their face.

clue.text: Crescent shape clear in stringed instrument

indicators.note: the clear sum goes inside the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument
to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: A crescent-shaped design shows plainly on a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' is the verb 'to net', as in clearing a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a half-moon or crescent-shaped object or space, from French for little moon.

clue.text: Traveller turned on lunatic

indicators.note: turned round, so the little word is read the other way

parts.note: lunatic and mad both mean crazy

explanation.surface: A traveller turns on someone and attacks them like a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place, a wanderer with no fixed home.

clue.text: European city not very European? This one is!

definitions.note: the answer is itself a European city, a French resort on the Riviera

indicators.note: not having the letters for 'very' and 'European', they are removed

parts.note: Venice is the Italian city of canals

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that some city doesn't feel very European, answered with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: Take V and E out of VENICE; the exclamation 'This one is!' says the remaining letters spell another European city.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation points back to 'European city': the leftover letters name a French Riviera resort.

clue.text: I travel uphill to find native

indicators.note: in a down clue going uphill means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to roam is to travel

explanation.surface: A traveller climbs a hill to meet a local.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, its native inhabitants.

clue.text: Aimless role conflated with half of next

indicators.note: conflated means fused together and mixed up
the first half of the following answer is taken

parts.note: the next down clue is 13 down, a five-and-five phrase

explanation.surface: A vague role gets muddled with half of what comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next' means the next down clue, 13 down; its first half, STUDY, is mixed with ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desultory means lacking a plan or purpose, going from one thing to another without aim.

clue.text: Unreliable parachute, not opened

indicators.note: not opened means without its opening letter

parts.note: a drogue is a small parachute used to slow or stabilise a larger one

explanation.surface: A skydiver's parachute fails to open and proves untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opened' looks like a failed parachute but removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rogue behaves erratically or dangerously, so it cannot be trusted.

clue.text: Use action mistaken as firm

indicators.note: the letters are taken wrongly, so put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A company's legal action is misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a business but is the adjective for holding on resolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious grip or person holds fast and will not let go, so is firm.

clue.text: They stop game animals getting to openings around rear of forest

indicators.note: the game animals go around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: deer are hunted as game

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: rents are tears or gaps

explanation.surface: Woodland deer reach gaps around the back of the forest and are stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterrents are things that discourage or prevent action, so they stop people doing it.

clue.text: Full of life, having given up, for some, the bottle

indicators.note: giving something up means doing without it, so it is removed

parts.note: vital means lively, full of life
in some Northern English dialects 'the' is shortened to t'

explanation.surface: Someone lively has given up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some, the' is T, the dialect t' of Yorkshire and Lancashire; 'having given up' removes it from VITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicine or perfume.

clue.text: "Macho man may finally behave like adult, ignoring women": researchers

parts.note: a stud is a sexually active virile man

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word
ignoring something means leaving it out

parts.note: to grow up is to act like an adult

explanation.surface: A quoted claim that a macho man may at last mature, which a set of researchers has been studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A study group is a team that studies a subject together, so its members are researchers.

clue.text: Hard to see through devious sort apprehended by US lawman

indicators.note: apprehended by means caught and held inside

parts.note: a Fed is an FBI agent

indicators.note: devious means following a twisting course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked character is arrested by an FBI agent, and is hard to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosted glass is treated to be translucent, so it cannot be seen through clearly.

clue.text: Recollection of showy defender

parts.note: flash means ostentatious, showy
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A footballer recalls a flamboyant defender.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashback is a sudden vivid memory of a past event, a recollection.

clue.text: Use up a colour in middle of neon

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the central letters
the middle of the word is its central two letters

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Instructions to exhaust one colour within a neon sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into resources is to consume them gradually, using them up.

clue.text: Cine scene reconstructed in ignorance

indicators.note: reconstructed means built again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film scene is restaged out of sheer ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for lack of knowledge, from Latin nescire, not to know.

clue.text: A British silver (not English) — get away!

indicators.note: not having the letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: silver is the medal for second place

explanation.surface: A British runner-up who isn't English is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver' is not the metal but second place, as in a silver medal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly or escape, to make a getaway.

clue.text: Stops enclosing excellent source of summer flowers

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: an engine dies when it stops
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as I

indicators.note: the source is the first letter

explanation.surface: Something halts and contains the best origin of summery blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excellent' is A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I. 'enclosing' makes 'Stops' wrap round it and the first letter of 'summer', the one 'source of' picks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisies are common small white-petalled blooms of lawns and meadows.

clue.text: Decorum in fashions? Totally gutted

parts.note: modes are fashions or styles

indicators.note: gutted means with the insides taken out, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether propriety is in fashion and is told they are thoroughly crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for 'devastated' but removes the inside of 'Totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is propriety in behaviour and dress, avoiding indecency.

clue.text: Is some misbehaving getting one imprisoned? That's an understatement

definitions.note: used here with 'an', a noun for the figure of speech

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so the letter is locked within
imprisoned means held inside, so the letter is locked within
misbehaving letters are disorderly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Saying some misbehaviour has landed someone in jail is putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, meiosis is deliberate understatement, as in litotes.

clue.text: A lot of sound about Uruguay's initial medal tally

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the letter
a lot of means most of, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: hale means healthy, sound in body

indicators.note: the initial is the first letter

explanation.surface: A hearty roar greets Uruguay's tally of medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of sound' looks like noise; it is most of HALE (healthy).
explanation.definitionFit: A haul is a large collection of winnings, so a team's medal tally.

clue.text: That woman will support American family in American story

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece holds up the one above it

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A woman will back an American family in some American tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The family is from Edgar Allan Poe's story 'The Fall of the House of Usher'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ushers, Roderick and Madeline, are the doomed family in Poe's tale.

clue.text: Quick statement about what to do if one's going to be late

definitions.text: statement about what to do if one's going to be late

parts.note: quick means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'
a will is a written statement of one's wishes

explanation.surface: A hurried note to say what to do if you're running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy, and 'Quick' means alive rather than fast.
explanation.definitionFit: This document sets out a person's wishes for medical care should they be dying and unable to decide.

clue.text: Flower in prominent position? Nothing revolutionary about that

indicators.note: about means around, so it surrounds the other piece
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nil means nothing
up means raised, on high

explanation.surface: A flower placed in a conspicuous spot is nothing radical.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Geographical feature unchanged with halves switched

indicators.note: the two halves of the word trade places

parts.note: unchanged means the same

explanation.surface: A landform stays the same even when its two halves swap over.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill with steep sides, common in the American southwest.

clue.text: Title cash disbursed in sporting event

indicators.note: disbursed means paid out, scattered around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prize money for a championship is paid out at a sports meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics covers track and field contests such as running, jumping and throwing.

clue.text: Confess it hurts having wordplay rejected

parts.note: ow is the cry of pain

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Someone admits it is painful having their joke turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit to something, to confess.

clue.text: Time to avoid backing US railways — there's fate to be suffered

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means leaving it out
backing means going in reverse

parts.note: Amtrak is the US national passenger rail service

explanation.surface: Choosing not to support American railways will bring retribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma is the consequence of one's own actions, destiny that must be borne.

clue.text: Pointlessly hard — hard and, yes, pain's involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Something tough and futile, and yes, it involves pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Sisyphus was condemned to push a boulder uphill forever, only for it to roll back each time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sisyphean task is laborious and never-ending, like the Greek myth's eternal punishment.
